$comment: Type checking for a codebase that is deliberately plain JavaScript.
CLAUDE.md asks for TypeScript strict mode on new work, and this repository is
41,000 lines of JS with no type layer at all — so neither the Definition of
Done nor the deploy gate could ever check the box that says 'type-check
clean'. Rewriting it would be weeks of risk for something the tests already
largely cover; `checkJs` gets most of the value for the price of this file.
Read it as a ratchet, not a wall. `npm run typecheck` compares against a
recorded baseline and fails only when the count goes *up*, so the debt is
frozen where it is and every new file has to be clean. That is the only
version of this that survives contact with a real backlog: a hard gate on day
one stops all other work until 400 pre-existing errors are cleared, and a
report nobody fails on is a report nobody reads.
Three flags are deliberately off, and one of them costs something worth
naming. `noImplicitAny` on untyped JS reports every parameter in the project
rather than anything wrong. `useUnknownInCatchVariables` accounted for 179 of
the first run's errors, every one a `catch (err) { err.message }` already
written defensively as `err?.message`.
`strictNullChecks` is the expensive one, and its absence is a real hole: with
it off, reading a property straight off `null` type-checks clean, which is the
single most common runtime bug there is. Measured on 2026-09-02, turning it on
takes the count from 429 to 1979. That is a project of its own and the next
one worth doing — until then, this checker catches property typos, wrong
arity and bad shapes, and does not catch null dereferences. Said plainly here
so nobody reads a green type-check as more than it is.
